card.name: Sentence ends in old historical prose
card.fires_on: Sentence-final periods and nearby linking words (it, were, is, that) after a completed clause in formal 19th-century style prose about history, politics, or nations.

modes.label: Period after a clause
modes.description: Full stop closing a sentence in historical or political writing.
modes.example: Our future connections with Spain and Spanish America will render that language of valuable acquisition<<.>> The ancient history of that part of America

modes.label: Linking word after a noun phrase
modes.description: A pronoun or verb right after a long subject noun phrase in older prose.
modes.example: the nobility to regain the independence<< it>> enjoyed in the Middle Ages, and the

card.plain: It marks the end of a sentence or clause in old-fashioned historical writing, just before a new one begins.
